title: I let Claude build my entire Balatro-inspired game. Then blud made a devlog roasting me
author: Top_West5024
selftext:
Babel's Ledger is a Balatro-inspired word incremental/roguelike: every page is random letters, real words score, and bookmarks multiply your score until the numbers get stupid.

I'm not a developer. My workflow was: play it on my phone, send Claude one-line notes ("lower the time a bit more", "make it vivid and dopamine hit"), repeat. 39 versions in about 34 hours, all in one HTML file.

Things that surprised me:

\- All 164 bookmark cards are drawn as SVG code. No image files at all, \~8,800 vector paths.

\- It can't feel if something is fun, so it wrote a bot that played 94 full runs overnight to balance the numbers.

\- Even the devlog is code: scenes in HTML/CSS rendered frame by frame, music and sound effects generated in Python, voice from ElevenLabs.

Demo coming soon. Happy to answer questions about the workflow.

Full devlog: [https://youtu.be/-QfkltDOoQY](https://youtu.be/-QfkltDOoQY)

itch page (demo soon): [https://promptpoweredgames.itch.io/babels-ledger](https://promptpoweredgames.itch.io/babels-ledger)

comments.author: WhosLive
comments.body: The overnight bot that plays full runs is the part most people skip. Since the AI can't feel fun, it usually helps to log a few stats per run (average run length, which cards get picked, where players die) and tell Claude to flag anything that wins too often or never gets chosen. Another thing worth trying is keeping a short design doc in the project that says what each card is supposed to feel like, so the balance passes don't flatten everything to the same power level over 39 versions.
